newsitem.title: INDIA: India Reliance starts petrochem cracker.
newsitem.headline: India Reliance starts petrochem cracker.

text.p: India's Reliance Industries on Monday said it had commissioned a new petrochemical cracker with an ethylene production capacity of 750,000 tonnes annually.
"RIL's (Reliance Industries Ltd) cracker is the only world scale ethylene plant in India," the firm said in a statement.
"It has the largest naphtha cracking capacity in Asia and is the first to be commissioned during the last 20 years in the country," it added.

The cracker is located at Reliance's Hazira Petrochemicals complex in the western state of Gujarat, and has a total production capacity of 2.2 million tonnes of various products annually, the statement said.

With the cracker on stream, Reliance said, its polymer, polyester and fabric businesses would be fully integrated. It is expected to improve Reliance's competitiveness by securing low stable cost raw materials by vertical backward integration.

"The cracker will substantially end Reliance's dependence on the international market for ethylene and propylene," the statement said. "It will also insulate the company from price fluctuations and will further save costs and enhance margins."
The company said it would use the cracker's entire production in the production of polyethylene, polypropylene, polyvinyl chloride and monoethylene glycol.
